clue.text: Mark moment

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a small check sign made against an item
second meaning: an instant, as in 'just a sec'

explanation.walkthrough: Mark reads like a name, but it is the first of two meanings; a tick is also British slang for a very short time.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names a checkmark on paper and also, informally in Britain, a brief instant of time.

clue.text: Sting held up crucifix to make a theatrical entrance

parts.note: a sting is a police trap to catch a crook

indicators.note: in a down entry, holding something up lifts it so it reads from bottom to top

parts.note: a rood is a cross or crucifix, as in a church rood screen

explanation.surface: The singer Sting hoists a crucifix aloft to make a dramatic stage entrance.
explanation.walkthrough: Sting looks like the rock star, but it is a police set-up.
explanation.definitionFit: A hinged opening in a stage floor lets an actor pop up suddenly, a classic way to arrive in pantomime.

clue.text: Broadcast saw a 22 in The Crucible

indicators.note: something broadcast is heard rather than read, so the words are judged by their sound

parts.note: spied is a past tense of see, spotted

explanation.surface: A broadcast shows someone spotting a rest during a play at The Crucible.
explanation.walkthrough: 22 is REST; The Crucible is the Sheffield theatre where world snooker is played, and a spider is a raised cue rest used to reach over balls.
explanation.definitionFit: In snooker a spider is a tall, arched rest that holds the cue above obstructing balls.

clue.text: Introduction to Leo Sayer CD remixed in a divine manner

indicators.note: a remix reorders and reworks a recording, so the letters are mixed into a new order
an introduction is the opening, so just the first letter of the next word is used

parts.note: the first letter of Leo
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A remixed CD by the singer Leo Sayer opens with a heavenly-sounding introduction.
explanation.definitionFit: Sacred means holy, belonging to God, so the adverb describes doing something in a holy, godly way.

clue.text: Brownie is one advanced artist

parts.note: came means moved forward or approached
RA is a Royal Academician

explanation.surface: A young Brownie Guide is singled out as one advanced artist.
explanation.walkthrough: Brownie looks like a junior Girl Guide; it is the Kodak Box Brownie, a cheap early snapshot device.
explanation.definitionFit: The Kodak Brownie was a famous inexpensive box model that made photography popular, so it is an example.

clue.text: Malt whiskey for son in class

indicators.note: one thing given for another means it is swapped in to take the other's place

parts.note: whiskey is W in the NATO phonetic alphabet
a sort is a kind or class
S is the standard abbreviation for son

explanation.surface: A malt whiskey is handed out in place of something for a son's class.
explanation.walkthrough: Malt whiskey reads as one drink, but whiskey is only the letter that replaces the son in a word meaning class.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the sweet liquid infused from mashed malted grain before fermentation in brewing, so malt extract.

clue.text: Hagrid confused over pressure and pH in this solution?

definitions.note: the two letters P and H together, sounding as one, are an example of the answer

indicators.note: a confused name has its letters muddled into a new order

parts.note: the Harry Potter gamekeeper, taken as written
P is the symbol for pressure in physics

explanation.surface: Hagrid is puzzled by pressure and pH readings in a chemistry solution.
explanation.walkthrough: Solution means the crossword answer, not a chemical liquid: the answer itself contains the letters PH, which spell one sound.
explanation.definitionFit: Two letters spelling a single sound, like ph in phone, form this; it is an example in the very word.

clue.text: Supermodel in endless pain after knockabout

indicators.note: after places the pain piece second, behind the turned-round knock
turning about faces the other way, so the word for knock runs backwards

parts.note: a rap is a sharp knock; the word's tail is the reversal signal

indicators.note: without its end, the final letter of the word pain's synonym is dropped

parts.note: agony is extreme pain

explanation.surface: A supermodel is left in pain after some rough-and-tumble.
explanation.walkthrough: Knockabout looks like one word for horseplay, but it splits into knock plus a reversal signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A perfect example or model of excellence is a paragon, so a 'super model' in the literal sense.

clue.text: Leave out captain

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to omit or pass over
second meaning: informal short form of skipper, a team or ship's leader

explanation.walkthrough: The second sense is a shortening of skipper, chiefly British for a team captain.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means to omit something, and the noun is a casual name for whoever leads a side or crew.

clue.text: Soap to turn off bloke

parts.note: to deter is to put someone off
gent is short for gentleman, a man

explanation.surface: A soap opera manages to put off some ordinary bloke.
explanation.walkthrough: Soap suggests a TV serial; here it is the cleaning product.
explanation.definitionFit: A cleaning agent such as washing powder or liquid is a synthetic kind of soap for laundry and dishes.

clue.text: 3 is natural at cooking

indicators.note: cooking mixes and transforms ingredients, so these letters are stirred into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone is a natural at cooking.
explanation.walkthrough: 3 points to the answer to 3-down, SPIDER.
explanation.definitionFit: This large hairy arachnid of the Americas is one particular kind of eight-legged creature named at 3-down.

clue.text: Romance from a special one — not half!

indicators.note: not half means only half of the name is kept, the rest dropped

parts.note: taken as written
José Mourinho, the football manager, called himself the Special One

explanation.surface: A romance with someone special is welcomed with the British exclamation 'not half!', meaning 'very much'.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not half!' sounds like enthusiastic British slang, but it instructs to keep only the first half of the manager's surname.
explanation.definitionFit: The French word for love is used in English for a love affair, often a secret one.

clue.text: Fighter entering a ring in China

indicators.note: a thing entering another goes inside it, so the fighter goes within the other pieces

parts.note: taken as written
O is ring-shaped
a MiG is a Russian fighter jet

explanation.surface: A boxer steps into a ring in China.
explanation.walkthrough: China is Cockney rhyming slang: china plate means mate. It looks like a country here.
explanation.definitionFit: The Spanish word for a friend matches china, rhyming slang for a pal or companion.

clue.text: Spooner's bottom tortures 3s

indicators.note: Spooner swapped the opening sounds of words, so the starts of the two words exchange

parts.note: a bed is the bottom of a river and racks are torture devices or acts of torturing

explanation.surface: Someone's backside is suffering agonies.
explanation.walkthrough: 3s means plural of 3-down, SPIDERs; swapping the B and R sounds turns the pair into Australian spiders.
explanation.definitionFit: These venomous Australian arachnids, with a red stripe on their bodies, are a species of 3-down.

clue.text: Conclusions from Sherlock Holmes surrounding unfortunate murders

indicators.note: surrounding something means wrapping around it, so one piece goes outside another
the conclusions of words are their endings, so only the final letter of each is taken

parts.note: the last letters of both names
ill as in ill luck, unlucky

explanation.surface: Sherlock Holmes reaches conclusions about some unfortunate murders.
explanation.walkthrough: Conclusions sounds like Holmes's deductions, but it means the final letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb meaning slays or puts to death fits murders in its third-person verb sense.

clue.text: Row involving Bond and Q's successor

parts.note: a tie is a bond or link
R follows Q in the alphabet

explanation.surface: A quarrel arises between James Bond and the successor to his gadget-maker Q.
explanation.walkthrough: Row suggests an argument and Bond the spy; Row is a line of seats and Bond is a tie.
explanation.definitionFit: A tier is one level in a series of seats or layers stacked above each other, so a row.

clue.text: I tucked into my bread

indicators.note: something tucked into another is pushed inside it

parts.note: taken as written
the Roman numeral I is one

explanation.surface: I tucked into my bread at mealtime.
explanation.walkthrough: Tucked into suggests eating; bread is slang for cash.
explanation.definitionFit: Bread is long-standing slang for cash, the stuff that buys your daily food.

clue.text: Animals make 22 distressed

indicators.note: distressed means troubled and shaken up, so these letters are disturbed into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
the answer to 22-across

explanation.surface: Animals make the remainder distressed.
explanation.definitionFit: These small burrowing mongooses of southern Africa, known for standing upright on sentry, are wild creatures.

clue.text: Issue returning for predator

indicators.note: returning means going back, so the word for issue is read backwards

parts.note: to issue is to flow out, as water from a spring

explanation.surface: A magazine issue is coming back to the newsstand for a predator.
explanation.definitionFit: This wild canine hunts in packs and preys on deer and livestock, a classic carnivore.

clue.text: Playing later in Court No.1

indicators.note: one piece placed in another sits inside it

parts.note: to court someone is to woo them

indicators.note: letters at play move around freely and settle in a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A tennis match is being played later on Court No.1 at Wimbledon.
explanation.walkthrough: Court No.1 is a Wimbledon show court, but No.1 is the definition: ABBA's Eurovision winner topped the British charts.
explanation.definitionFit: ABBA's 1974 Eurovision-winning song reached the top spot of the British singles chart, so a chart-topper.

clue.text: Diver succeeded opening his knife?

indicators.note: the letter for succeeded opens up the knife word and goes inside it

parts.note: couteau is French for knife; his because the diver was French
S abbreviates succeeded in genealogies

explanation.surface: A diver succeeded in prising open a knife.
explanation.walkthrough: Jacques Cousteau, the French undersea explorer, would call his knife by the French word.
explanation.definitionFit: Jacques-Yves Cousteau was a pioneering underwater explorer who co-invented the Aqua-Lung scuba apparatus.

clue.text: Meagre royalties ultimately accepted by Prince Harry?

indicators.note: something accepted by another is taken inside it

parts.note: Spare is the title of Prince Harry's memoir, and he is the spare to the heir

indicators.note: ultimately means finally, so only the last letter of the word is kept

parts.note: the last letter of royalties

explanation.surface: Prince Harry accepts only meagre royalties from his book.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that Prince Harry stands for his memoir, not the man.
explanation.definitionFit: Thin, scanty or scarcely spread out describes something meagre in quantity.

clue.text: Article reduced in M&S for little kids

indicators.note: placed in another, the shortened word sits inside it

parts.note: taken as written, the two letters around the ampersand

indicators.note: reduced means cut down, so the word loses its last letter

parts.note: an item is an article or object

explanation.surface: A reduced-price article at M&S, the British store Marks & Spencer, is for small children.
explanation.definitionFit: Mites are small creatures or tiny children, an affectionate term for little ones.

clue.text: Ray cut short 50% of I Say a Little Prayer

indicators.note: cut short means the end is chopped off, so the final letter goes

parts.note: the manta is a large ray

indicators.note: fifty percent of a word is half of it, so only its first two letters stay

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone shortens the song I Say a Little Prayer, recorded by Dionne Warwick.
explanation.walkthrough: The song title splits, and its tail is the definition: the praying insect is a small creature that seems to pray.
explanation.definitionFit: The praying insect holds its forelegs together as if in devotion, so it is jokingly a tiny worshipper.

clue.text: Small man from BP?

parts.note: surface reading: a minor employee of the oil company
setter's reading: in chess notation B and P stand for a dark-side piece of lowest rank; chess pieces are called men

explanation.walkthrough: BP looks like British Petroleum, the oil company; it is chess shorthand, where a man is a piece and the smallest is a pawn.
explanation.definitionFit: A chessman of the lowest value on the dark side, written BP in old descriptive notation.

clue.text: Power breakfast served up including cup of tea

indicators.note: in a down entry, served up means sent upward, so the letters read bottom to top
the phrase includes the answer within its run of letters

parts.note: the letters spanning the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: A power breakfast is served with a cup of tea.
explanation.definitionFit: A brew is British informal for a pot or mug of tea, as in 'fancy a brew?'.

clue.text: Take it easy in nature study

indicators.note: in signals letters lying inside the following words

parts.note: the end of nature joined to the start of study

explanation.surface: Someone relaxes by doing a little nature study.
explanation.definitionFit: To relax or stop working for a while is what taking it easy means.

clue.text: Shakespearean actor finishes in plays with Laurence Olivier

indicators.note: finishes are endings, so the final letter of each following word is used

parts.note: the last letters of the four words

explanation.surface: A Shakespearean actor finishes his run of plays alongside Laurence Olivier.
explanation.walkthrough: Antony Sher was a leading Royal Shakespeare Company actor, famous as Richard III.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Antony Sher was a celebrated stage performer best known for his roles with the Royal Shakespeare Company.

clue.text: fifteensquared.net is one place to see Arachne's work?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: fifteensquared is an online blog explaining crossword answers
second meaning, read in two parts: Arachne, a weaver turned into a spider in Greek myth, spins a web, and a site is a place

explanation.walkthrough: Arachne is also a Guardian setter, whose puzzles are discussed on fifteensquared; the question mark marks the split reading.
explanation.definitionFit: An internet address like fifteensquared.net hosts a set of online pages, and a spider's web location fits the split reading.

clue.text: Former husband more generous claims old wife

indicators.note: to claim something is to take hold of it, so one piece grips the others inside

parts.note: wider means broader or more liberal
O is the abbreviation for old
W is the abbreviation for wife

explanation.surface: A more generous ex-husband lays claim to his old wife.
explanation.walkthrough: Former husband suggests divorce, but here the marriage ended with the wife's death.
explanation.definitionFit: A man whose spouse has died, and who has not remarried, was once a husband.
